root_cause.text: The metadata compression code path uses direct `return` statements instead of proper cleanup via `goto` labels, causing folio reference leaks when validation errors occur in metabox-enabled EROFS images.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces two `return -EFSCORRUPTED;` statements with `goto out;` in the metabox validation section of `erofs_read_superblock()`. The direct returns bypass necessary cleanup code that would be executed at the `out` label, leading to unreleased folio references when crafted images trigger these validation failures. The commit message explicitly states "incorrect early returns, leading to folio reference leaks" and the fix was introduced after the metadata compression feature (commit 414091322c63) was added.

intent_record.intent_summary: Refactor error handling in metabox validation to use centralized goto-based cleanup path instead of early returns.
intent_record.what: Replaced two direct `return -EFSCORRUPTED;` statements with `goto out;` statements within the metabox validation block. Added `ret = -EFSCORRUPTED;` assignment before the conditional checks to set the error code that will be returned via the goto label.
intent_record.how: This change converts early returns into a centralized error handling path using a goto statement. Instead of returning immediately on validation failures, the code now sets the error code and jumps to an `out` label (presumably defined later in the function) for cleanup and unified exit. This enables proper resource cleanup or finalization logic that would be bypassed by early returns.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function contains direct `return` statements at lines 325 and 328 within the metabox validation code path, instead of using `goto out` for proper cleanup. When these validation errors occur (lines 325: 'if (sbi->sb_size <= offsetof...)' and line 328: 'if (sbi->metabox_nid & BIT_ULL...)'), the function returns immediately without executing the cleanup code at line 351 (`erofs_put_metabuf(&buf)`). This causes a folio reference leak from the `erofs_read_metabuf()` call at line 261. All other validation errors in the function properly use `goto out` (lines 271, 277, 281, 288, 296, 303, 339), but the metabox-specific checks bypass this cleanup mechanism.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function properly uses goto-based cleanup throughout. All validation error paths (lines 268, 274, 278, 285, 293, 300) use 'goto out;' which ensures the cleanup code at lines 335-337 executes, calling erofs_put_metabuf(&buf) before returning. The early return at line 261 occurs before buf is initialized via erofs_read_metabuf, so no leak occurs there. The compression parsing at line 326 and device scanning at line 331 also properly use 'goto out;' on error. The vulnerable construct described (direct returns instead of goto cleanup) is not present in this code - proper cleanup via goto labels is already implemented.
